questions.text: Which German subject pronoun means «we»?

feedback: Ihr means you (talking to several friends)

questions.solution: Wir = we; ihr = you (plural, informal), sie = they or she, du = you (one friend)
questions.hint: Its verb forms usually end in -en, just like the infinitive

questions.text: What does «nie» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.always: Always is immer; nie is a negative

questions.solution: Nie (or niemals) = never; immer = always
questions.hint: It is the opposite of immer

questions.text: What does «nichts» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Nichts = nothing; etwas = something
questions.hint: It is the opposite of etwas

questions.text: Give the «ich» form of «sein» in the present tense. Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Sein: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie sind
questions.hint: Sein is irregular: think of how you say «I am» in German

questions.text: Give the «er» form of «haben» in the present tense. Type the verb only.

feedback.ist: Ist comes from sein; this question asks for haben

questions.solution: Haben: ich habe, du hast, er hat, wir haben, ihr habt, sie haben
questions.hint: Haben loses its b in the du and er forms

questions.text: In the nominative, which word means «the» before a plural noun such as «Bücher»?

feedback: Der is masculine singular in the nominative
Das is neuter singular
Dem is dative singular

questions.solution: In the nominative and accusative, all plural nouns take die: die Bücher
questions.hint: In the plural, all three genders share the same article

questions.text: Which word means «my» before a feminine noun such as «Schwester» (nominative)?

feedback: Mein is for masculine or neuter nouns
Deine means your

questions.solution: Feminine nouns take meine: meine Schwester
questions.hint: Feminine possessives add -e

questions.text: Choose the correct article: «___ Mädchen ist nett.»

feedback: Mädchen is neuter, not feminine

questions.solution: Mädchen is neuter (all nouns ending in -chen are neuter): das Mädchen
questions.hint: Nouns ending in -chen are always neuter

questions.text: Which sentence means «I have a brother»?

feedback: Bruder is masculine and the object, so ein must change to einen
Einem is dative; haben needs the accusative

questions.solution: Haben takes the accusative; masculine ein becomes einen: Ich habe einen Bruder
questions.hint: The object of haben is in the accusative, and Bruder is masculine

questions.text: Translate into German. Include the definite article (der, die or das): the girl

feedback.die Mädchen: Die Mädchen is the plural; one girl is neuter

questions.solution: Mädchen is neuter: das Mädchen
questions.hint: German nouns ending in -chen are neuter

questions.text: Give the plural of «das Buch», with its article.

feedback.die Buche: Die Buche is a beech tree

questions.solution: Das Buch → die Bücher (umlaut + -er)
questions.hint: Many neuter nouns add -er in the plural, sometimes with an umlaut

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Ich fahre mit ___ Bus.»

feedback: Den is accusative; mit takes the dative
Bus is masculine, and mit takes the dative

questions.solution: Mit always takes the dative; Bus is masculine: mit dem Bus
questions.hint: Mit is always followed by the dative case

questions.text: Complete with the correct form of «mein»: «Ich besuche ___ Onkel.» Type the missing word only.

feedback.mein: Onkel is masculine and the object of besuchen, so it is accusative
feedback.meinem: Meinem is dative; besuchen takes the accusative

questions.solution: Besuchen takes an accusative object; Onkel is masculine: meinen Onkel
questions.hint: Onkel is masculine and it is the direct object

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Meine Schwestern ___ groß.»

feedback: Ist goes with a singular subject
Seid goes with ihr

questions.solution: A plural subject takes sind; adjectives after sein (like groß) do not change
questions.hint: Schwestern is plural (sie)

questions.text: What does «Ich esse nie Fleisch» mean?

options: I am not eating meat today
I eat a lot of meat

questions.solution: Nie = never, Fleisch = meat: I never eat meat
questions.hint: Look at the word straight after the verb

questions.text: What does «Wir werden einen Film sehen» mean?

options: We would like to watch a film
We watch a film every day

questions.solution: Werden + infinitive at the end = future: we will watch a film
questions.hint: Werden + an infinitive at the end talks about the future

questions.text: Read: «Gestern habe ich mit Paul Tennis gespielt.» When did this happen? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Gestern = yesterday
questions.hint: Look at the first word of the sentence

questions.text: Read: «Lena trinkt nie Kaffee.» What does Lena never drink? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Kaffee = coffee: Lena never drinks coffee
questions.hint: Look at the noun at the end

questions.text: Which sentence is in the perfect tense (Perfekt)?

feedback: Werde ... spielen is the future
Möchte ... spielen means would like to play

questions.solution: Perfekt = haben/sein + past participle at the end: ich habe gespielt
questions.hint: Look for a past participle starting with ge- at the end

questions.text: Read: «Ich mag kein Gemüse.» What does the speaker dislike? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Kein Gemüse = no vegetables; Gemüse = vegetables
questions.hint: Carrots and peas are examples

questions.text: Complete with the Perfekt: «Gestern ___ wir nach Berlin gefahren.» Type the missing verb only.

feedback.haben: Verbs of movement like fahren take sein in the Perfekt
feedback.ist: Ist goes with er/sie/es; the subject here is wir
feedback.waren: Waren is the simple past of sein; the Perfekt needs the present of sein

questions.solution: Fahren (movement) takes sein: wir sind gefahren
questions.hint: Verbs of movement form the Perfekt with sein

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «fahren»: «Mein Bruder ___ gern Rad.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Fahren adds an umlaut with du and er/sie/es: er fährt
questions.hint: Fahren is a strong verb: its vowel changes with er

questions.text: Which sentence means «I play football because it is fun»?

options: Ich spiele Fußball, weil es macht Spaß
Ich spiele Fußball, weil macht es Spaß
Ich spiele Fußball, weil es Spaß macht
Ich spiele Fußball, weil Spaß es macht

questions.solution: Weil sends the verb to the end of its clause: weil es Spaß macht
questions.hint: Weil is a conjunction that moves the verb to the end

questions.text: Choose the correct word order: «Am Wochenende ___ ins Kino.»

feedback: After a time phrase at the start, the verb comes before the subject

questions.solution: The verb comes second: Am Wochenende gehe ich ins Kino
questions.hint: The verb must be the second idea in the sentence

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «müssen»: «Ich ___ heute meine Hausaufgaben machen.» Type the verb only.

feedback.müssen: Müssen is the infinitive or the wir/sie form
feedback.musste: Musste is the simple past (had to)

questions.solution: Müssen with ich: ich muss (no umlaut in the singular)
questions.hint: Modal verbs lose their umlaut in the singular

questions.text: Choose the correct form of «aufstehen»: «Ich ___ morgen früh auf.»

feedback: In a main clause the prefix separates and goes to the end
Steht goes with er/sie/es

questions.solution: Separable verb: the prefix auf goes to the end: ich stehe morgen früh auf
questions.hint: Aufstehen is separable, and the prefix is already at the end

questions.text: Which sentence in the Perfekt is correct?

options: Sie hat gestern in die Stadt gefahren
Sie ist gestern in die Stadt gefahren
Sie ist gestern in die Stadt gefahrt
Sie ist gestern in die Stadt fahren

questions.solution: Fahren takes sein and its participle is gefahren
questions.hint: Check the auxiliary and the past participle

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «I would like to travel to Spain»?

feedback: The infinitive must go to the end of the sentence
Ich bin ... gereist means I travelled

questions.solution: Möchte + infinitive at the end: Ich möchte nach Spanien reisen
questions.hint: After a modal verb, the infinitive goes to the end

questions.text: Which negative sentence is correct?

options: Ich habe nicht gelesen das Buch
Ich nicht habe das Buch gelesen
Ich habe das Buch gelesen nicht
Ich habe das Buch nicht gelesen

questions.solution: Nicht comes before the past participle at the end: Ich habe das Buch nicht gelesen
questions.hint: The past participle always stays at the very end

questions.text: Translate into German using the Perfekt: «they went» (on foot)

feedback.sie sind gegeht: Gehen is irregular: its participle is not gegeht

questions.solution: Gehen takes sein and has the irregular participle gegangen
questions.hint: Gehen is a verb of movement with an irregular past participle

questions.text: Translate into German using werden + infinitive: «I will eat»

feedback.ich esse: That is the present; this question asks for werden + infinitive
feedback.ich wird essen: Wird goes with er/sie/es; with ich use werde

questions.solution: Future: ich werde + infinitive at the end: ich werde essen
questions.hint: Use the ich form of werden, then the infinitive

questions.text: Translate into German using würde + infinitive: «we would play»

feedback.wir werden spielen: Wir werden spielen is the future (we will play)
feedback.wir würde spielen: With wir, the form is würden

questions.solution: Conditional = würden + infinitive: wir würden spielen
questions.hint: Use the wir form of würde, then the infinitive

questions.text: What does «der Bruder» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Der Bruder = the brother (plural: die Brüder)
questions.hint: Think of the boys in a family

questions.text: What does «die Tante» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.uncle: Uncle is der Onkel; die Tante is female

questions.solution: Die Tante = the aunt
questions.hint: She is your mother's or father's sister

questions.text: Which is the German for «grandfather»?
questions.solution: Der Großvater (or Opa) = grandfather; die Großmutter = grandmother, der Enkel = grandson, der Onkel = uncle
questions.hint: Groß + the word for father

questions.text: What does «der Arzt» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Der Arzt / die Ärztin = the doctor
questions.hint: This person treats people who are ill

questions.text: Which word means «tired»?
questions.solution: Müde = tired; glücklich = happy, krank = ill, böse = angry
questions.hint: Think of how you feel after a long day

questions.text: What does «das Frühstück» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Das Frühstück = breakfast
questions.hint: It's the first meal of the day

questions.text: Which word means «funny»?
questions.solution: Lustig = funny; schüchtern = shy, faul = lazy, ernst = serious
questions.hint: This person makes you laugh

questions.text: False friend! What does «das Gymnasium» mean in English? Answer in English.

feedback.gym: False friend: das Gymnasium is an academic secondary school
feedback.gymnasium: False friend: das Gymnasium is an academic secondary school
feedback.sports hall: False friend: a sports hall is die Turnhalle

questions.solution: Das Gymnasium is an academic secondary school, like a grammar school
questions.hint: It's a false friend: pupils study there for the Abitur

questions.text: Which is the feminine form of «der Lehrer» (the teacher)?
questions.solution: Add -in for a woman: der Lehrer → die Lehrerin
questions.hint: Many job words add -in for a woman

questions.text: Translate into German. Include the definite article (der, die or das): the sister
questions.solution: Schwester is feminine: die Schwester
questions.hint: Is a sister masculine, feminine or neuter?

questions.text: Which sentence means «I get up at seven o'clock»?

options: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf
Ich gehe um sieben Uhr ins Bett
Ich wache um sieben Uhr auf
Ich ziehe mich um sieben Uhr an
feedback: Ins Bett gehen means to go to bed
Ich wache auf means I wake up, not I get up
Ich ziehe mich an means I get dressed

questions.solution: Aufstehen = to get up; aufwachen = to wake up, ins Bett gehen = to go to bed, sich anziehen = to get dressed
questions.hint: Which separable verb means to get out of bed?

questions.text: Translate into German. Include «ein» or «eine»: a nurse (a woman)

feedback.ein Krankenpfleger: Ein Krankenpfleger is a male nurse

questions.solution: Eine Krankenschwester (or eine Krankenpflegerin) = a female nurse
questions.hint: It is a compound noun starting with krank (ill)

questions.text: Choose the correct form: «Ich habe ___ Haare.» (long)
questions.solution: With no article, plural adjectives in the accusative end in -e: lange Haare
questions.hint: Haare is plural and has no article in front

questions.text: What does «die Augen» mean?
questions.solution: Die Augen = the eyes; die Ohren = ears, die Haare = hair, die Zähne = teeth
questions.hint: You see with them

questions.text: What does «Mein Vater ist größer als meine Mutter» mean?

options: My father is older than my mother
My mother is taller than my father
My father is as tall as my mother
My father is taller than my mother

questions.solution: Größer als = taller than: my father is taller than my mother
questions.hint: Groß + -er + als makes a comparison

questions.text: Read: «Mein Bruder ist sehr gesprächig.» What is the brother like? Answer in English with one word.
questions.solution: Gesprächig = chatty or talkative
questions.hint: It is related to sprechen (to speak)

questions.text: Read: «Meine Tante ist Rechtsanwältin.» What is the aunt's job? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Rechtsanwältin = lawyer (a woman)
questions.hint: Recht means the law

questions.text: What does «Ich muss mein Zimmer aufräumen» mean?

options: I have to tidy my room
I want to tidy my room

questions.solution: Ich muss = I must / I have to; aufräumen = to tidy up
questions.hint: Muss comes from müssen

questions.text: Read: «Um fit zu bleiben, esse ich Obst und rauche nicht.» What does the speaker do to stay healthy?

options: Eats fruit and does not smoke
Drinks water and does not smoke

questions.solution: Ich esse Obst = I eat fruit; ich rauche nicht = I don't smoke
questions.hint: Find the two verbs: esse and rauche

questions.text: Read: «Morgens dusche ich und trinke Tee.» What does the speaker drink in the morning? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Ich trinke Tee = I drink tea
questions.hint: It's a hot drink, often served with milk in Britain

questions.text: Complete with the reflexive pronoun: «Ich wasche ___ jeden Morgen.» Type the missing word only.

feedback.sich: Sich goes with er, sie, es or sie (they); with ich use the ich pronoun
feedback.mir: Mir is dative; here the accusative is needed

questions.solution: The reflexive pronoun for ich (accusative) is mich: ich wasche mich
questions.hint: Which reflexive pronoun goes with ich?

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Meine Schwester ___ Ärztin werden.» (wants to)

feedback: Willst goes with du
Wollen goes with wir or sie (they)
Wollt goes with ihr

questions.solution: Wollen with sie (she): sie will
questions.hint: Meine Schwester = sie (she)

questions.text: Complete with the correct form of «mein»: «Ich wohne mit ___ Mutter.» Type the missing word only.

feedback.meine: Mit takes the dative; feminine meine becomes meiner
feedback.meinem: Meinem is for masculine or neuter nouns; Mutter is feminine

questions.solution: Mit takes the dative; Mutter is feminine: mit meiner Mutter
questions.hint: Mit is always followed by the dative

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Nächstes Jahr ___ mein Bruder an die Uni gehen.» (will)

feedback: Werde goes with ich
Werden goes with wir or sie (they)
Wirst goes with du

questions.solution: Future with er: er wird + infinitive at the end
questions.hint: Mein Bruder = er

questions.text: Complete with the simple past (Präteritum) of «sein»: «Als ich klein ___, wohnte ich in Köln.» Type the verb only.

feedback.waren: Waren goes with wir or sie (they)

questions.solution: Präteritum of sein with ich: ich war
questions.hint: Sein has an irregular simple past of just three letters

questions.text: Choose the correct auxiliary: «Heute Morgen ___ ich um sechs Uhr aufgewacht.»

feedback: Aufwachen takes sein, not haben
Ist goes with er/sie/es; the subject is ich

questions.solution: Aufwachen (a change of state) takes sein in the Perfekt: ich bin aufgewacht
questions.hint: Verbs that show a change of state, like waking up, use sein

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.solution: Eltern is plural: meine Eltern sind; an adjective after sein (nett) does not change
questions.hint: Check the possessive, the verb and the adjective

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «When I am older, I would like to be a vet»?

options: Wenn ich älter bin, ich möchte Tierarzt werden
Wenn ich bin älter, möchte ich Tierarzt werden
Wenn ich älter bin, möchte ich Tierarzt werden
Als ich älter war, wollte ich Tierarzt werden
feedback: Als ich älter war means when I was older

questions.solution: Wenn sends bin to the end; the main clause then starts with its verb: möchte ich
questions.hint: Wenn sends the verb to the end, and the main clause starts with its verb

questions.text: Which negative sentence is correct?

options: Ich nie gehe spät ins Bett
Nie ich gehe spät ins Bett
Ich gehe nie spät in Bett
Ich gehe nie spät ins Bett

questions.solution: The verb stays second, nie follows it, and ins = in das: Ich gehe nie spät ins Bett
questions.hint: The verb must be the second idea

questions.text: Translate into German: «she is tall and intelligent»

feedback.sie ist große und intelligente: Adjectives after sein do not take endings
feedback.sie sind groß und intelligent: Sie sind means they are; she is = sie ist

questions.solution: Adjectives after sein take no endings: sie ist groß und intelligent
questions.hint: After ist, adjectives keep their basic form

questions.text: Translate into German using werden + infinitive: «I will work»

feedback.ich arbeite: That is the present; this question asks for werden + infinitive

questions.solution: Ich werde + infinitive at the end: ich werde arbeiten
questions.hint: Use the ich form of werden, then the infinitive

questions.text: Translate into German: «my brothers are lazy»

feedback.meine Brüder sind faule: Adjectives after sein do not take endings
feedback.mein Bruder ist faul: That is singular (my brother is lazy)

questions.solution: Plural: meine Brüder sind faul (Bruder → Brüder)
questions.hint: Bruder takes an umlaut in the plural; adjectives after sein don't change

questions.text: What does «das Schwimmen» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Das Schwimmen = swimming (schwimmen = to swim)
questions.hint: It's a sport you do in a pool

questions.text: What does «der Käse» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Der Käse = cheese
questions.hint: It's made from milk; you might put it on a sandwich

questions.text: Which is the German for «the mobile phone»?
questions.solution: Das Handy = the mobile phone; die Fernbedienung = the remote control
questions.hint: It looks like an English word, but English does not use it for this

questions.text: What does «das Schach» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Schach spielen = to play chess
questions.hint: A board game with kings, queens and knights

questions.text: Which word means «the cake»?

feedback: Die Küche is the kitchen

questions.solution: Der Kuchen = the cake; die Küche = the kitchen, das Brot = bread, der Fisch = fish
questions.hint: You might have one with candles on your birthday

questions.text: What does «das Lied» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Das Lied = the song
questions.hint: You sing it

questions.text: Which word means «Christmas»?
questions.solution: Weihnachten = Christmas; Ostern = Easter, der Geburtstag = birthday, Silvester = New Year's Eve
questions.hint: In Germany it is celebrated on 24–26 December

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Ich ___ gern Rad.» (I like cycling)

feedback: Spielen is used for games and instruments

questions.solution: Rad fahren = to cycle: ich fahre gern Rad
questions.hint: In German you «drive» a bike

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Ich gehe gern ___ Kino.»

feedback: Im (dative) shows position, not movement
In den is for masculine or plural nouns; Kino is neuter singular

questions.solution: Movement into a place takes the accusative; Kino is neuter: in das = ins
questions.hint: Movement towards a place uses the accusative; Kino is neuter

questions.text: Translate into German. Include the definite article (der, die or das): the music
questions.solution: Musik is feminine: die Musik
questions.hint: Most nouns ending in -ik are feminine

questions.text: Translate into German. Include the definite article (der, die or das): the newspaper
questions.solution: Zeitung is feminine, like all nouns ending in -ung: die Zeitung
questions.hint: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine

questions.text: Which word means «cartoons»?
questions.solution: Zeichentrickfilme = cartoons; Seifenopern = soap operas, Spielshows = game shows, Nachrichten = the news
questions.hint: Zeichnen means to draw

questions.text: What does «die Nachrichten» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Die Nachrichten = the news
questions.hint: A programme about what happened in the world today

questions.text: Which sentence means «I like reading»?
questions.solution: Verb + gern = to like doing something: ich lese gern
questions.hint: Put gern straight after the verb

questions.text: What does «Ich sehe lieber Horrorfilme» mean?
questions.solution: Verb + lieber = prefer: I prefer watching horror films
questions.hint: Verb + lieber shows a preference

questions.text: Read: «Am Samstag gehe ich mit meiner Schwester ins Schwimmbad.» On which day does the speaker go to the pool? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Am Samstag = on Saturday
questions.hint: It's the day before Sonntag

questions.text: Read: «Mein Lieblingsessen ist Brathähnchen.» What is the speaker's favourite food? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Brathähnchen = roast chicken
questions.hint: Hähnchen is a bird you eat; braten is a way of cooking it

questions.text: What does «Ich verbringe zu viel Zeit in den sozialen Medien» mean?

options: I spend too much time on social media
I spend very little time on social media
I spent a long time on my phone

questions.solution: Zeit verbringen = to spend time; zu viel = too much; die sozialen Medien = social media
questions.hint: Zu viel means too much

questions.text: Read: «Zum Geburtstag haben mir meine Eltern eine Gitarre geschenkt.» What present did the speaker get? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Eine Gitarre = a guitar
questions.hint: It's a musical instrument with strings

questions.text: Read: «Ich mag Rap nicht, aber ich liebe Jazz.» Which statement is true?

options: The speaker likes both rap and jazz

questions.solution: Ich mag Rap nicht = I don't like rap; ich liebe Jazz = I love jazz
questions.hint: Aber (but) separates the two opinions

questions.text: Complete with the past participle of «sehen»: «Letztes Wochenende haben wir einen tollen Film ___.» Type the past participle only.

feedback.gesehnt: Gesehnt comes from sich sehnen (to long for)
feedback.sehen: Use the past participle, not the infinitive

questions.solution: Sehen has the participle gesehen: wir haben ... gesehen
questions.hint: Strong verbs form the participle with ge- ... -en

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: «Morgen ___ wir ins Kino gehen.» (want to)

feedback: Will goes with ich or er/sie/es
Willst goes with du
Wollt goes with ihr

questions.solution: Wollen with wir: wir wollen + infinitive at the end
questions.hint: The subject is wir: which ending matches the infinitive?

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «lesen»: «Mein Vater ___ jeden Tag die Zeitung.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Lesen changes e → ie with du and er: er liest
questions.hint: Lesen is a strong verb: its vowel changes with er

questions.text: Choose the correct pronoun: «Magst du den Film? — Ja, ich finde ___ toll.»

feedback: Es replaces a neuter noun; Film is masculine
Ihm is dative; finden needs an accusative object

questions.solution: Film is masculine and it is the object, so the accusative pronoun is ihn
questions.hint: Film is masculine, and the pronoun is the object

questions.text: Complete with the simple past (Präteritum) of «haben»: «Früher ___ ich keinen Computer.» Type the verb only.

feedback.hatten: Hatten goes with wir or sie (they)

questions.solution: Präteritum of haben with ich: ich hatte
questions.hint: Früher = in the past; haben is irregular in the simple past

questions.text: Which sentence means «I think that the film is good»?

options: Ich denke, dass der Film gut ist
Ich denke, dass der Film ist gut
Ich denke, dass ist der Film gut
Ich denke, dass gut der Film ist

questions.solution: Dass sends the verb to the end: dass der Film gut ist
questions.hint: Dass is a conjunction that moves the verb

questions.text: Which sentence about last night is correct?

options: Gestern Abend haben wir ins Konzert gegangen
Gestern Abend sind wir ins Konzert gegangen
Gestern Abend wir sind ins Konzert gegangen
Gestern Abend sind wir ins Konzert gegeht

questions.solution: Gehen takes sein (participle gegangen), and the verb comes second after the time phrase
questions.hint: Check the auxiliary, the word order and the participle

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «I don't like playing computer games»?
questions.solution: Nicht gern = do not like doing: ich spiele nicht gern Computerspiele
questions.hint: Nicht goes in front of gern

questions.text: Which sentence with «wenn» (if) is correct?

options: Wenn ich Geld hätte, ich würde eine Konsole kaufen
Wenn ich hätte Geld, würde ich eine Konsole kaufen
Wenn ich Geld hätte, würde ich eine Konsole gekauft
Wenn ich Geld hätte, würde ich eine Konsole kaufen

questions.solution: Wenn sends hätte to the end; the main clause starts with würde, and kaufen goes to the end
questions.hint: Watch the word order in both halves of the sentence

questions.text: Translate into German: «I play the guitar»

feedback.ich spielt Gitarre: With ich, the verb ends in -e: spiele

questions.solution: Ich spiele Gitarre (German usually leaves out the article with instruments)
questions.hint: Use the ich form of spielen

questions.text: Translate into German using the Perfekt: «she watched a film»

accept: sie hat sich einen Film angesehen
sie hat sich einen Film angeschaut

feedback.sie hat ein Film gesehen: Film is masculine and the object, so einen
feedback.sie hat gesehen einen Film: The past participle goes to the end

questions.solution: Sehen takes haben; Film is masculine accusative (einen); the participle goes to the end
questions.hint: Sehen uses haben, and Film is masculine

questions.text: Translate into German: «we are going to the restaurant»

feedback.wir gehen im Restaurant: Im shows position; movement into a place needs ins (accusative)
feedback.wir gehen in dem Restaurant: Movement into a place needs the accusative: in das (ins)
feedback.wir geht ins Restaurant: With wir, the verb is gehen

questions.solution: Movement into a place takes the accusative: in das = ins Restaurant
questions.hint: Movement into a place uses the accusative

questions.text: What does «der Strand» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Der Strand = the beach
questions.hint: You find sand and the sea there

questions.text: What does «der Bahnhof» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Der Bahnhof = the (railway) station
questions.hint: You catch a train there

questions.text: Which is the German for «it is raining»?
questions.solution: Es regnet = it is raining; es schneit = it is snowing, es ist sonnig = it is sunny, es ist windig = it is windy
questions.hint: Think of der Regen (rain)

questions.text: What does «die Bäckerei» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Die Bäckerei = the bakery (der Bäcker = the baker)
questions.hint: You buy bread and rolls there

questions.text: Which word means «the plane»?
questions.solution: Das Flugzeug = the plane; das Schiff = the ship, das Auto = the car, der Reisebus = the coach
questions.hint: Fliegen means to fly

questions.text: What does «das Rathaus» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Das Rathaus = the town hall
questions.hint: The mayor (der Bürgermeister) works there

questions.text: Which word means «the bedroom»?
questions.solution: Das Schlafzimmer = the bedroom; die Küche = the kitchen, das Badezimmer = the bathroom, das Wohnzimmer = the living room
questions.hint: Schlafen means to sleep

questions.text: False friend! What does «der Rock» mean?

feedback: False friend: a rock is der Felsen or der Stein

questions.solution: False friend: der Rock = the skirt; a rock is der Felsen or der Stein
questions.hint: It's an item of clothing

questions.text: Translate into German. Include the definite article (der, die or das): the library
questions.solution: Die Bibliothek (or die Bücherei) = the library; a bookshop is die Buchhandlung
questions.hint: It is feminine, and it is not the word for a bookshop

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Die Bank ist ___ dem Kino.» (next to)

feedback: Gegenüber means opposite
Hinter means behind

questions.solution: Neben = next to; gegenüber = opposite, hinter = behind, unter = under
questions.hint: This preposition shows that something is beside something else

questions.text: Translate into German. Include the definite article (der, die or das): the car
questions.solution: Auto is neuter: das Auto (der Wagen also means car)
questions.hint: Is Auto masculine, feminine or neuter?

questions.text: Choose the correct word: «Ich fahre ___ Spanien.» (to Spain)

feedback: In + dative means in a country, not going to it
Zu is used for people and buildings

questions.solution: Travelling to most countries and towns uses nach: nach Spanien
questions.hint: Most countries without an article use the same preposition as towns

questions.text: What does «die Kreuzung» mean in English? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Die Kreuzung = the crossroads (junction)
questions.hint: It's where two roads cross

questions.text: Which word means «on the left»?

feedback: Rechts means on the right
Geradeaus means straight on

questions.solution: Links = on the left; rechts = on the right, geradeaus = straight on, gegenüber = opposite
questions.hint: It is the opposite of rechts

questions.text: What does «Es ist heiß und sonnig» mean?
questions.solution: Heiß = hot; sonnig = sunny
questions.hint: Sonnig contains the word Sonne (sun)

questions.text: Read: «Ich fahre mit dem Rad zur Schule.» How does the speaker travel to school? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Mit dem Rad = by bike
questions.hint: It has two wheels and pedals

questions.text: Read: «Letzten Sommer bin ich mit meiner Familie nach Italien gefahren.» Which country did the speaker visit? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Italien = Italy
questions.hint: Its capital is Rome

questions.text: What does «Der Bahnhof ist gegenüber der Bank» mean?

options: The station is opposite the bank
The station is next to the bank
The station is behind the bank
The bank is opposite the post office

questions.solution: Gegenüber = opposite: the station is opposite the bank
questions.hint: Gegenüber is a preposition of place: think of facing something

questions.text: Read: «In meiner Stadt gibt es zu viel Verkehr.» What problem does the town have? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Der Verkehr = traffic: there is too much traffic
questions.hint: Think of cars, buses and lorries on the roads

questions.text: Read: «Um die Umwelt zu schützen, recycle ich und fahre mit dem Bus.» What does the speaker do?

options: Saves water and takes the bus
Turns off the lights and recycles

questions.solution: Ich recycle = I recycle; ich fahre mit dem Bus = I go by bus
questions.hint: Find the two verbs after um die Umwelt zu schützen

questions.text: Complete with the past participle of «fliegen»: «Meine Eltern sind gestern nach Rom ___.» Type the past participle only.

feedback.fliegen: Use the past participle, not the infinitive
feedback.gefliegt: Fliegen is a strong verb: its participle ends in -en with a vowel change

questions.solution: Fliegen is a strong verb: sie sind geflogen
questions.hint: Fliegen is irregular: the vowel changes in the past participle

questions.text: Choose the correct ending: «Wenn das Wetter morgen schön ist, ___»

feedback: After a wenn clause, the verb must come straight after the comma

questions.solution: After a wenn clause, the main clause starts with the verb: …, fahren wir an den Strand
questions.hint: The whole wenn clause counts as the first idea, so the verb comes next

questions.text: Complete with the present tense of «nehmen»: «Mein Vater ___ den Zug nach Berlin.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Nehmen is irregular: er nimmt
questions.hint: Nehmen changes its vowel and doubles a consonant with er

questions.text: Choose the correct adjective ending: «Ich wohne in einem ___ Haus.» (big)

feedback: Großes is used after ein in the nominative or accusative; einem is dative

questions.solution: After einem (dative), the adjective ends in -en: in einem großen Haus
questions.hint: In + dative shows position; adjectives after einem end in -en

questions.text: Complete with the simple past (Präteritum) of «regnen»: «Im Urlaub ___ es jeden Tag.» Type the verb only.
questions.solution: Regular verb in the simple past: es regnete
questions.hint: Regular verbs add -te in the simple past

questions.text: Which sentence means «I bought it yesterday» (it = das T-Shirt)?

feedback: Ihn replaces a masculine noun
Sie replaces a feminine or plural noun
Ihm is dative

questions.solution: T-Shirt is neuter (das T-Shirt), so the pronoun is es
questions.hint: Das T-Shirt is neuter

questions.text: Which sentence about last year is correct?

options: Letztes Jahr haben wir nach Spanien gefahren
Letztes Jahr sind wir nach Spanien gefahren
Letztes Jahr wir sind nach Spanien gefahren
Letztes Jahr sind wir nach Spanien fahren

questions.solution: Fahren takes sein, the verb comes second, and the participle gefahren goes at the end
questions.hint: Check the auxiliary, the word order and the participle

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «We must protect the environment»?
questions.solution: Müssen + infinitive at the end: Wir müssen die Umwelt schützen
questions.hint: After a modal verb, the infinitive goes to the end

questions.text: Read: «Früher gab es ein Kino in meinem Dorf, aber jetzt gibt es nichts mehr.» Which statement is true?

options: There is a new cinema in the village
There has never been a cinema in the village
The cinema is going to close soon
There used to be a cinema, but now there is nothing

questions.solution: Früher gab es = there used to be; jetzt gibt es nichts mehr = now there is nothing any more
questions.hint: Compare früher (in the past) with jetzt (now)

questions.text: Translate into German using the Perfekt: «I went to the beach»

accept: ich bin an den Strand gegangen
ich bin an den Strand gefahren
reject: ich habe an den Strand gegangen
ich bin an dem Strand gegangen

feedback.ich bin an dem Strand gegangen: Movement needs the accusative: an den Strand
feedback.ich bin am Strand gegangen: Am Strand shows position; movement needs an den Strand

questions.solution: Gehen and fahren take sein; an den Strand (accusative) or zum Strand shows movement
questions.hint: Use sein, and remember that movement takes the accusative

questions.text: Translate into German using werden + infinitive: «it will rain»

feedback.es regnet: Es regnet is the present (it is raining)

questions.solution: Es wird + infinitive: es wird regnen
questions.hint: Use the es form of werden, then the infinitive

questions.text: Translate into German: «there is a lot of traffic»

feedback.es gibt viele Verkehr: Verkehr is uncountable, so use viel, not viele

questions.solution: Es gibt = there is; Verkehr is uncountable, so viel (not viele)
questions.hint: Use es gibt, and the word for a lot that goes with an uncountable noun
